recipes.name: Chicken and Cheese Stuffed Jumbo Shells
ingredients_raw: 4 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves - cubed

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Add pasta and cook for 8 to 10 minutes or until al dente; drain. Separate shells and let stand, so they are not touching, on waxed paper or foil.

In large skillet over medium heat, combine chicken, onion, egg and bread crumbs. Cook until chicken is no longer pink. Season with oregano, basil, salt and pepper. Stir in three-quarters of the shredded mozzarella and cheddar; cook until cheeses melt.

Fill shells with chicken mixture, using a tablespoon, and place in a 9 x 13 baking dish. Cover the shells with the tomato sauce and top with the reserved cheese. Cover with foil and bake 45 minutes, or until lightly browned and bubbly.

raw_recipe.headline: Chicken and Cheese Stuffed Jumbo Shells
raw_recipe.description: Jumbo pasta shells stuffed with chicken and cheese, and baked in tomato sauce.

review.reviewBody: Can't give it 5 stars, because I made a lot of changes. But I use most recipes as a base, anyway. Used 2 chicken breasts, simmered in olive oil with crushed garlic and italian seasoning until done. Put the chicken in a blender on 'salsa' to chop it up (much easier than tearing with forks!). Added the oil (which was about 1/8 cup), 1/2 c bread crumbs, 15oz ricotta, 1/2 c mozz, 1/4 c parmesean and mixed together. Used 1/2 box of shells, boiled and stuffed, then refridgerated for the next day. I get home much later than my boyfriend, so it was convenient to just pour jarred alfredo and some mozz, throw it in the oven for 30 mins.

The recipe is a good base but there's much more potential with this (it takes more time but is very much worth it). For the mixture, I used boneless, skinless chicken thighs and omitted the onion (it's in my homemade sauce). Used 1 clove of garlic, basil, oregano, thyme, and some garlic chives from the garden as it cooked. Removed from pan so as not to cook the egg. Replace 1/2 of bread crumbs with parmesan cheese. Add 1/2 cup of cottage cheese. Omit the cheeses from the mixture and replace cheddar and all mozzarella for topping.

With a homemade sauce from San Marzano garden tomatoes, this was an impressive recipe. Sure, making your own sauce is extra time, but so worth it. 

I appreciate this recipe giving me ideas on how to stuff the shells. I stuffed extra shells with pepperoni, roasted cherry tomatoes, and cubed cheese. That was amazing as well.

I already had cooked chicken, so I cubed it up, threw in 2 cloves of garlic and onion using the shredding and pulsing button on my food processer. Since I didn't have cheddar cheese I used about a half of cup of parmesan cheese I did put in a kettle for a bit to heat the egg up, then stuffed the shells, layered pepperoni over them then cheese. baked until finished... was so yummy! :D

I didn't care for the method used to cook the chicken. I liked the taste of the final product although I did modify the ingredients. I sautéed the chicken with butter and garlic and seasoned with Chinese five spice. Just a pinch of the five spice though because of the strong flavor that it produces. I added 10 ounces of ricotta cheese to the finished chicken dish and only placed shredded cheese on top of the filling after the shells were filled. I used a pasta sauce that was already seasoned because the plain tomato sauce leaves a tart and sour flavor with no additional seasonings added. Turned out great with some modifications.

I used this recipe as a base and made some modifications. It turned out very well. I sauted the onion and chicken with garlic in olive oil. when the chicken was about done I added the spices and then shredded the ckicken. I also took one beaten egg, 1/2 cup of cottage cheese (all out of ricotta) and 1/4 cup of parmesan cheese and mixed that with the chicken mixture. Stuffed the shells and topped it with tomato-cream sauce for pasta from this site. Will make again.

This is incredibly delicious. A few changes that I made: I cooked the onion (and added a few cloves of minced garlic) in oil in a saute pan for a couple minutes, added the chicken, which I had chopped very small, and allowed those ingredients to cook through. I then mixed together the egg and the bread crumbs, and added the cheese. I only used 1/2 a box of shells, and it was the perfect amount. Also, I used one can of Bertolli Tomato and Basil sauce along with one can of Del Monte chopped tomatoes (with basil and oregano), as opposed to the 29 oz. can of tomato sauce. This is definitely a keeper.

I thought this looked boring as is so I changed it up. I boiled chicken and shredded it. I mixed it with spinach, rictta cheese, parm cheese, salt, pepper, garlic powder, and nutmeg. I then added one beaten egg and mixed everything together and stuffed manicotti shells with the mixture and put homemade marinara sauce and topped with mozzarella and parm cheeses. I baked until nice and crusty and got rave reviews. I saved 2 shells with mixture and froze to save for next time to make with alfred sauce instead of the red sauce. Thanks for the recipe...you can be very creative with this.

I used other reviewers suggestions and simmered the chicken in olive oil, garlic, and italian seasonings. I used fresh basil and oregano in the filling and also added about 1.5 oz cream cheese to the mixture. I made a whole box of shells and froze half of them for another time. Very good! thanks for the recipe!
I liked using the chicken. I blended it in my Ninja and added some rocatta cheese. That made it easier to stuff into the shells.

Good recipe, but I a few of alterations. I cut out the egg and used some olive oil instead. I cooked the onion and the chicken, along with a couple garlic cloves in a skillet. When the chicken was nearly fully cooked I added the basil, oregano, salt and pepper and sauted for a bit longer. I them removed that from the pan into a bowl and added the cheese. I didn't like the idea of putting cheese into a hot skillet (seems like too much of a mess to me). The cheese melted perfectly and I mixed that, along with some fresh Parmesan. Filled the shells, and put them into a pan and used nearly 3x the sauce, added the cheese and I baked for 25 covered and 10 uncovered. I'm not sure how it would of turned out without these changes, but my boyfriend raved about this and demands it on at least a bi-weekly basis.

We loved this recipe!! My kids and husband ate it up. I was a little concerned about the egg cooking in the skillet so I cooked the chick and onion (with some garlic) first and stirred the breadcrumbs (panko) and egg in at just before the cheese. Then like others, I added a small container of ricotta. I also used pasta sauce instead of tomato sauce. It was good. I didn't have any problem with the shells getting hard ... The texture was perfect. I would serve this to company and there is enough for my family of four to eat a second meal.
Added ricotta cheese instead of other cheeses. It needed a little something more but was pretty good.
Seasoned the ricotta with Italian seasoning, garlic powder, and season salt. Amazing! Family favorite
Every one loved it, only change was half the onion.
No and yes....
I prepared it per directions, and my family loved it
Followed the exact recipe. Will not be making this again. Very bad taste and texture, and the spices did not incorporate well into the dish

My absolute favorite recipe! I was a little unsure about the egg until everything was done, but well worth it. I used seasoned bread crumbs instead of adding the oregano and basil and added the bread crumbs and egg after the chicken was cooked. If you like chicken cheese and pasta you will love this!!

I used ground chicken and added 2 minced cloves of garlic. Cooking everything together made the filling a little mushy. I should have cubed the chicken like the recipe like the recipe calls for, but I thought the chicken cubes would be a little bland. I would recommend adding the bread crumbs slowly to just coat the chicken lightly - they added to the mushy filling. Overall, this recipe is a nice change from the usual ricotta & spinach stuffing or ground turkey.

Stuffing was too dry & needed more seasoning so I added almost a full container of Ricotta cheese, approx. 1/2 cup sour cream, some other Italian seasonings, & next time would add some diced tomatoes instead of just tomato sauce. I didn't have regular mozzarella cheese so I chopped string cheese. Delicious!
